title: First ionisation energy, lithium to argon
caption: Ionisation energy rises across each period as nuclear charge grows with similar shielding, and falls sharply at each new period. The small dips at boron and aluminium (a new p sub-shell) and at oxygen and sulfur (the first paired p electron) are evidence for sub-shells.
alt: Line graph of first ionisation energy for elements 3 to 18, rising across period 2 to neon, dropping to sodium, rising again to argon, with dips at B, O, Al and S.
description: Period 2: lithium 520 rising to neon 2081 kJ mol⁻¹, with dips at boron (801, below beryllium 899) and oxygen (1314, below nitrogen 1402).
Sodium drops to 496: a new shell.
Period 3 repeats the pattern, with dips at aluminium (578) and sulfur (1000), up to argon 1521.
